title: Workload capsule (capsule_bench_v0)
description: A compiler-input workload capsule: describes what to compile, the numeric golden policy, the expected Gemmini instruction coverage, the required oracle tiers, and the public/dev/hidden label. A capsule is an INPUT to the backend-under-test, never a kernel.

source_role.description: where this capsule came from. derived_sweep = expanded from a profile's declared tile-relative sweep, so its shapes track the target's geometry rather than being written down; the sweep's prose is carried in source_reference along with the tile the extents resolved against; model_derived = the shape came from a real application the user declared, so it is deliberately NOT tile-relative -- it is the geometry that model actually contains, and it carries the class and the cost basis it was sized against in source_reference; smt_counterexample = the shape and inputs came from a solver counterexample that refuted a translation-validation obligation, so the witness is generated by the verifier rather than chosen by an author -- see docs/design/compiler_verification.md

source_reference.description: bareMetalC path / torch module slice / ISA section / local spec id

role.description: Operand role. 'scale' is a block-scale stream: a microscaling operand is a PAIR -- quantized elements plus one shared exponent per fixed-length block of them -- so a block-scaled capsule declares its scales as operands a backend can be handed, rather than leaving them reachable only by the reference kernel.

dtype.description: Element type of this tensor. Not a fixed enum: the numeric-format vocabulary is data, declared in merlin/schemas/quant_formats.registry.yaml (where a new format -- MX, NVFP4, a GGUF k-quant -- is an entry, not a code change), so a list copied here goes stale the moment a target brings a format the list predates. Validity is enforced by merlin.targetgen.contract.schemas.validate_capsule against that registry plus plain machine accumulator widths, and an unknown token is still a hard ContractViolation.

scale_of.description: For a 'scale' operand: the operand whose blocks it scales. Names the pairing explicitly so a backend need not infer it from operand order.

block.description: For a 'scale' operand: how many elements of the scaled operand share one exponent, along the contraction axis. Derived from the target's declared scale group, never assumed -- a different microscaling profile uses a different run length.

op.description: The workload the capsule asks the backend to compile. Unlike dtype this IS a closed set, because an op is only expressible if the tooling can build its interface MLIR and produce its golden -- the vocabulary is code, not data. Its sources are merlin.targetgen.corpus_spec.BUILDERS (capsule + interface MLIR) and capsule_golden._recompute_golden (integer goldens; float ops carry an independent golden.yaml instead). Adding a builder without adding it here rejects the whole corpus at load, which is why merlin/tests/targetgen/test_capsule_vocabulary.py pins this list against BUILDERS.

dtype.description: Element type the golden comparison is performed in. Same open vocabulary as inputs[].dtype -- see that field.

instruction_classes.description: Required instruction classes, DERIVED per-target from the target's own ISA (e.g. gemmini RoCC classes, or a self-hosted ISA's semantic op patterns like MXUMatMul/TensorBaseOffset). Not a fixed enum: the class vocabulary is the target's, so validity is enforced by the per-target derivation (isa_taxonomy) + its coverage checker, not a hardcoded list here.

modes.description: Coverage axes this capsule exercises, as {mode: true}. Open for the same reason instruction_classes is: a mode names a datapath feature of the target under test, so the vocabulary belongs to the corpus and its target, not to this file. The closed list this replaced was gemmini's eight (i8/relu/acc_scale/k_accumulate/resident_reuse/conv2d/movement/padded_edge) and it rejected radiance's whole corpus over `rmsnorm: true`. coverage_report keeps those eight as the BASELINE always-reported axes so a 0 stays an explicit 'not covered' row, and unions in whatever else a corpus declares rather than dropping it.

max_oracle_tier.description: Deepest oracle tier this capsule will be graded at -- a per-capsule CEILING. Tiers deeper than this are recorded as `skipped` with a reason naming the ceiling and the budget behind it; the key is NEVER omitted, because a tier with no record is not evidence (not_run_is_not_pass) and an absent key reads as though the capsule was never graded. Exists because certification cost is measured and grows with a capsule's depth (merlin.targetgen.cert_cost fits it per target/tier/engine from the runs already on disk), so a capsule too expensive to certify is screened at the cheap tier instead of silently costing hours. A capped capsule SHOULD also declare `extends`, naming the sibling that carries the deeper certification; a ceiling without one is a strictly weaker claim and is recorded as such. Enforced at grade time by merlin.targetgen.tier_policy.oracle_ceiling.

max_timing_tier.description: Deepest tier bought for this capsule's TIMING measurement -- an exclusion from the measurement matrix, deliberately a DIFFERENT field from `max_oracle_tier`. A tier is bought for one of two reasons and a ceiling on one must never silence the other: `max_oracle_tier` caps CORRECTNESS (the capsule is screened cheaply and its correctness rests on an `extends` sibling), while a performance claim NEEDS the cycle-accurate count on whatever rung the capsule's own acceptance block names in `performance.acceptance.evidence.timing_tier`. Capping correctness therefore does NOT decline the timing rung, or a cell that was measured would read back as though it never was. Declare this only to state that a member is genuinely not to be measured at that rung; the tier is then recorded as `skipped` with `measurement_excluded: true`, which is a statement about the measurement matrix and NOT a correctness verdict.

extends.description: Name of the SIBLING capsule whose deeper oracle-tier certification this capsule rests on. The honesty mechanism for `max_oracle_tier`: a capped capsule is not 'uncertified', it is 'screened at the cap and resting on <this sibling>'s certification'. Declared on the capsule rather than inferred from a naming convention, so what the claim rests on is readable from the capsule itself and auditable after the fact.

pass_requirements.description: Target-independent compiler requirement classes this capsule must exercise.

verilator.description: Availability of the cycle-accurate Verilator RTL-cert tier (L3). optional = graded when the sim is available but NOT a pass-gate; the mandatory numeric tier is whatever the capsule lists in required_oracle_tiers (e.g. L2 = a functional oracle). A prototype/not-RTL-certified target sets this optional so an unavailable/slow RTL sim never forces incomplete.

semantic.description: Target-conditioned semantic-coverage annotations (Acceleratable Region Recall). semantic_family is the canonical computation family this capsule exercises (derived from operation.op when omitted); eligible is an author override of the independent eligibility oracle (auto = derive); must_accelerate makes a fallback on an eligible region a FAIL; generalization_axis records which held-out axis this capsule probes.

not_asserted_reason.description: why must_accelerate is NOT asserted: the demand could not be grounded in the target's own capabilities, so no acceleration is required of a submission. Recorded rather than left implicit — an absent must_accelerate reads identically whether the author decided against it or the derivation failed.

composed_families.description: Families this capsule exercises IN COMPOSITION with semantic_family, derived from its epilogue. A target may declare a family reachable only when fused (composed_with), which makes a standalone capsule for it the wrong capsule -- the eligibility oracle refuses one as a false fallback -- so a fused capsule is the only thing that can ever evidence that cell. Crediting a capsule for exactly one family left such a cell permanently uncoverable while the requirement kept demanding it.

composed_families_unresolved.description: Epilogue stage names whose family could not be resolved. Recorded rather than dropped: silently withholding coverage a capsule earned is the failure composed_families exists to fix, and an unmapped stage name is exactly how that would recur.

gate.description: Scheduling gate: a whole-model capsule is only run once the op-level suite has proven itself. `after_op_pass_fraction` is the minimum fraction of graded op capsules that must PASS before this capsule is scheduled.

lanes.description:
INTEROP contract. `require` names the execution lanes that must each have carried work, using the routing plan's own keys (e.g. `on_mesh`, `in_contract_vector_scalar`, `scalar_rvv_lane`). A capsule that names lanes asserts COMPOSITION across backends -- part of the model on the accelerator, part on the scalar/vector lane the target also owns -- so work reaching the other lane is the behaviour under test, not a fallback failure. `semantic.must_accelerate` is withheld for such a capsule for the same reason, unless it explicitly reclaims it. A named lane the routing plan does not report fails the capsule with that lane named.

`forbid` is the NEGATIVE case and the content of a host-only capsule: lanes that must have carried NOTHING, because the target's capability manifest does not admit this capsule's family and accelerating it would be as wrong as failing to accelerate admitted work. It is honoured ONLY against execution evidence, never a routing plan -- 'the router planned no work here' is not 'the compiler put no work here', and this is the direction in which a plan-only pass is most dangerous. A lane may not appear in both lists.

A capsule must name at least one of `require` or `forbid`. `require` alone is a composition assertion; `forbid` ALONE is a pure negative and is the honest shape for a synthesized host-only capsule -- adding a `require` for the host lane would demand evidence no op-path grade can produce, making the capsule a permanent `incomplete` instead of a test. The negative is enforceable on its own: a decoded accelerator instruction violates it.
